rounds.gap: The strip landing spot (blank plaster between the SPEX photo and the right column, about x 1300-1560) has nothing marking it and the window-transom shadow ends in a soft dark smudge across its middle, so it reads as a hole in the cluster rather than an inviting reserved place: mark it (for example a waiting piece of masking tape plus faint pencil corner ticks) and keep it in clean sunlight.
rounds.notes: Name, Liew riso offset, note and chips all sit in full sun and are crisp (the note is better lit than in the bar); 5 papers + 2 stickers, within budget; nothing clipped; no console errors. Top chrome now falls in shadow: KUCHING, SARAWAK sits inside the mullion shadow (about 1.8:1, lit in the bar) and SCRAPBOOK N 12 is near-illegible in the dark top-right corner (about 1.2:1). Contact shadows are faint: the SPEX photo and ADMIT ONE ticket show almost no shadow under their bottom edges and no lifted corner, so they read slightly printed-on, and the cream ticket barely separates from the wall. URIIS 2026 label sits in the transom shadow (legible but dim). SCROLL TO TAKE A PHOTO says what happens next but is small, low contrast (about 2.9:1) and far from the spot. Overall frame is slightly brighter and creamier than the rose-amber bar.

rounds.gap: The blown-out window sits inside the left-40% caption column at every card stop and slides further left as the flight goes on, so its white panes wash out caption text (line ends in SPEX, BuildUp, kacha and HaoJia; most of the titles and kickers in Herbarium, Cloud architecture on AWS, Bar and Little Lemon); keep the window right of the caption column at every stop.
rounds.notes: Cards not fully in frame at several stops: the SPEX and BuildUp cards run off the right edge (BuildUp's TOP 5 stamp is cut), and at HaoJia, Herbarium and Bar the card just passed hangs in front as a huge out-of-focus beige slab over the right 25-35% of the frame, cutting the current card ('herbarium proje', only ~60% of Bar shows). Strengths: warm window glow, volumetric beam with dust, taped polaroids with handwritten captions and gloss, good near/far depth from the stack of upcoming cards, cards never cross into the caption column, framing settles at each stop with no visible whip, no console errors.
